topicName: Garbage Collectors (G1, ZGC, Shenandoah) Tuning and Selection
content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Garbage Collectors (G1, ZGC, Shenandoah) Tuning and Selection in Java"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Choosing and tuning the right Garbage Collector (GC) is crucial for meeting latency and throughput SLAs in modern enterprise Java applications. This tutorial explores the characteristics, use cases, and tuning strategies for the three primary production-grade collectors: G1, ZGC, and Shenandoah."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Understanding the Garbage Collectors"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"G1 (Garbage-First): The default collector since Java 9. Designed for multi-processor large memory heaps. It aims to meet a configurable pause time goal with high throughput."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"ZGC (Z Garbage Collector): A scalable low-latency garbage collector designed for heaps ranging from megabytes to terabytes. Pause times do not increase significantly with heap size, usually staying below a millisecond."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Shenandoah: An ultra-low-latency garbage collector that does concurrent compaction, providing low pause times independent of the heap size by running evacuation simultaneously with the running Java threads."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Selection Criteria: Which Collector to Choose?"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Selection depends heavily on your application's memory size and latency requirements:"},{"order":9,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use G1 if your heap is moderate (e.g., 4GB to 32GB) and your application can tolerate pauses in the range of 10ms to 200ms while prioritizing maximum overall throughput."},{"order":10,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use ZGC if you have a massive heap (32GB to multi-terabytes) and require strict, predictable ultra-low pause times (less than 1ms) for latency-sensitive applications like financial trading systems."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Use Shenandoah if you are running on OpenJDK, require low pause times similar to ZGC, and prefer a collector that performs well across a wider range of heap sizes without requiring extreme hardware."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Enabling the Garbage Collectors"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"To enable ZGC or Shenandoah, you must pass specific flags to the JVM startup command, as G1 remains the default."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"java -XX:+UseZGC -jar my-application.jar"},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"java -XX:+UseShenandoahGC -jar my-application.jar"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Tuning G1 Garbage Collector"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"G1 tuning revolves around setting pause time targets and managing the initiation of mixed collections."},{"order":18,"type":"code","text":"java -XX:+UseG1GC -XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200 -XX:InitiatingHeapOccupancyPercent=45 -jar my-application.jar"},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-XX:MaxGCPauseMillis=200: Sets a soft goal for maximum GC pause time. The JVM will adjust the work done per collection to meet this target."},{"order":20,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-XX:InitiatingHeapOccupancyPercent=45: Percentage of the total heap occupied to trigger a concurrent marking cycle. Lower this if concurrent cycles start too late and full GCs occur."},{"order":21,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Tuning ZGC"},{"order":22,"type":"paragraph","text":"ZGC requires very little tuning compared to older collectors. Most parameters are self-adjusting. However, managing allocation rates and thread counts is sometimes necessary."},{"order":23,"type":"code","text":"java -XX:+UseZGC -XX:ConcGCThreads=4 -XX:+UnlockDiagnosticVMOptions -jar my-application.jar"},{"order":24,"type":"bullet_point","text":"-XX:ConcGCThreads: Sets the number of concurrent garbage collection threads. Adjust this based on available CPU cores to balance background GC CPU usage with application throughput."},{"order":25,"type":"subheading","text":"6. Tuning Shenandoah"},{"order":26,"type":"paragraph","text":"Shenandoah supports multiple heuristics (such as adaptive, compact, and stw) which determine when cycles are triggered."},{"order":27,"type":"code","text":"java -XX:+UseShenandoahGC -XX:ShenandoahGCHeuristics=adaptive -jar my-application.jar"},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"adaptive: Dynamically adjusts GC frequency based on allocation rates and available free memory."},{"order":29,"type":"subheading","text":"7. Monitoring and Diagnostics"},{"order":30,"type":"paragraph","text":"Always enable unified JVM logging to analyze garbage collection performance in production environments."},{"order":31,"type":"code","text":"java -Xlog:gc*,gc+phases=debug:file=gc.log:time,uptime,pid:filecount=5,filesize=100M -jar my-application.jar"}]
